title: Back then
job: Habits and states in the past; then against now
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

rules.text: THE IMPARFAIT CAN CARRY A WHOLE PERIOD ON ITS OWN. L2-M10 and L3-M10 used it to paint the scene a story happened in; here there is no story around it. j'habitais à Paris is not a moment in a tale — it is a stretch of life that is over. Nothing is newly conjugated: the endings are L2-M10's and this module does not touch them.

THE CONTRAST NEEDS A NOW HALF, OR IT IS NOT A CONTRAST. Autrefois, j'habitais à Paris. Maintenant, j'habite ici. The imparfait alone says a thing was so; putting a present clause beside it is what says it has stopped. Write the pair, and let the two time words — autrefois or à l'époque against maintenant or aujourd'hui — carry the whole meaning.

ENGLISH MARKS PAST HABIT TWICE AND FRENCH MARKS IT NOT AT ALL. English has used to and it has would — we used to go, we would go every summer. French has NEITHER: on allait is the whole of it. The learner will keep hunting for a word to translate used to, will not find one, and will start bolting extra verbs on. There is nothing to add.

ONE ENGLISH would, TWO FRENCH TENSES. We would go every summer is a HABIT and takes the imparfait: on allait. I would go if I could is a HYPOTHESIS and takes L3-M4's conditional: j'irais. English spells them the same and French never does. The only test is the question: is this sentence about something that used to happen, or about something that has not happened at all?

ne … plus IS NOT ANY MORE, AND IT KEEPS ITS ne. Je ne fume plus, on ne se voit plus. It is the negator for a thing that stopped, and like every other negator it is written with its ne (docs/58 §4). Careful: L2-M9's plus is the comparative — plus facile, more easy. Same four letters, opposite jobs, and only the ne in front of the verb tells them apart.

THE TIME WORD IS WHAT DOES THE WORK. autrefois, à l'époque and the bare adverb avant all open a period, and once one is in place the imparfait needs no help. That avant is the SAME word L3-M8 taught in front of a date (avant le cinq) — one key, two jobs, and no second row is opened for it here.

sentences.display: Autrefois, j'habitais à Paris. Maintenant, j'habite ici
sentences.cue: I used to live in Paris. Now I live here
sentences.literal: Formerly, I-lived at Paris. Now, I-live here

words.note: Opens a period that is finished. One word, and once it is in place the imparfait behind it needs no further marking.
The imparfait of habiter, with L2-M10's endings unchanged. The elision makes it one word and one key, as j'étais and j'avais are.
The now half of the pair. Without it the first clause says only that something was true, not that it has stopped being true.
The present beside the imparfait. Putting the two forms of one verb side by side is the clearest shape this module has.

sentences.trap: English needs used to here and French has no word for it. A learner who insists on translating it reaches for a second verb and produces something French has no room for.
sentences.sound: oh-truh-FWAH, zha-bee-TEH ah pah-REE. man-tuh-NAHN, zha-BEET ee-SEE. The -ais of j'habitais is an open eh; j'habite ends on a clipped t.

variations.display: Autrefois, je travaillais à Paris. Maintenant, je travaille ici
variations.cue: I used to work in Paris. Now I work here
variations.changed: another verb through the same two-tense pair

variations.display: Autrefois, j'habitais ici. Maintenant, j'habite à Paris
variations.cue: I used to live here. Now I live in Paris

mistake.display: Autrefois, j'ai habité à Paris. Maintenant, j'habite ici
mistake.why: the passé composé makes it one finished event, as if you lived there once and it was over in an afternoon. A stretch of life takes the imparfait.

sentences.usage: Answering where are you from? with the honest two-part version instead of one place name.
sentences.mnemonic: Then in the imparfait, now in the present.

sentences.display: À l'époque, on n'avait pas de voiture
sentences.cue: Back then, we didn't have a car
sentences.literal: At the-time, one not-had not of car

words.note: Names a period rather than a moment. It is the phrase a French speaker reaches for first when they mean back when things were different.
Written whole because n'avait is its own elided key. The pattern under it is L2-M10's avait, negated, with pas de for the absent thing.

sentences.trap: English says we didn't have a car and puts the past on did. French puts it on the verb itself — n'avait — and there is no auxiliary anywhere in the sentence to carry it.
sentences.sound: ah lay-POK, ohn na-VEH pah duh vwah-TEWR. on n'avait links across the n, so it comes out as one run, ohn-na-veh.

variations.display: À l'époque, on n'avait pas de voiture ici
variations.cue: Back then, nobody here had a car
variations.changed: the place is named at the end

variations.display: Autrefois, on n'avait pas de voiture
variations.cue: In the old days, we didn't have a car

mistake.display: À l'époque, on n'a pas eu de voiture
mistake.why: the passé composé says the car failed to turn up on one occasion. A standing state — not owning one, for years — is the imparfait's job.

sentences.usage: Explaining how a household or a town used to work, to somebody who was not there.
sentences.mnemonic: A state that lasted is imparfait.

sentences.display: Quand j'étais petit, je jouais dehors
sentences.cue: When I was little, I played outside
sentences.literal: When I-was small, I played outside

words.note: Taken whole: every piece is already owned — quand and j'étais are L2-M10's, petit is L2-M2's — and it is the standard opener for a childhood.
The imparfait of jouer on L2-M10's endings: -ais, -ait, -ions. Nothing here is new but the stem.
Outside in the open air, with no place named after it. The final s is silent.

sentences.trap: I played and I used to play are two English sentences; je jouais is the only French one. Reaching for the passé composé here — j'ai joué — turns a whole childhood into one afternoon.
sentences.sound: kahn zhay-TEH puh-TEE, zhuh zhoo-EH duh-OR. jouais is two syllables ending on an open eh; the s of dehors is not sounded.

variations.display: Quand j'étais petit, je jouais avec mes amis
variations.cue: When I was little, I played with my friends

variations.display: Quand j'étais petit, on jouait dehors
variations.cue: When I was little, we played outside
variations.changed: the subject, and the ending moves with it

mistake.display: Quand j'étais petit, j'ai joué dehors
mistake.why: j'ai joué is one occasion of playing. A childhood habit is a repeated stretch, and French marks that on the verb: je jouais.

sentences.usage: The opening line of every story anybody has ever told about their own childhood.
sentences.mnemonic: A habit repeats, so the imparfait does.

sentences.display: Avant, on allait au cinéma tous les jours
sentences.cue: We used to go to the cinema every day
sentences.literal: Before, one went to-the cinema all the days

words.note: The third-person imparfait of aller. Its first person, allais, is L2-M10's and stays there — this row opens only the cell that module left empty.

sentences.trap: The bare avant here is the same word L3-M8 taught in front of a date. Used alone at the head of a clause it means back then, and English speakers who learnt it as before will read it as incomplete.
sentences.sound: ah-VAHN, ohn na-LEH oh see-nay-MAH too lay ZHOOR. on allait links across the n; tous les jours runs as three flat syllables.

variations.display: Avant, on allait au marché tous les jours
variations.cue: We used to go to the market every day

variations.display: À l'époque, on allait au cinéma tous les jours
variations.cue: Back then, we used to go to the cinema every day

mistake.display: Avant, on est allés au cinéma tous les jours
mistake.why: on est allés is one trip that happened. tous les jours says it happened over and over, and a repeated trip takes the imparfait: on allait.

sentences.usage: Describing what a place or a family used to do with its evenings.
sentences.mnemonic: tous les jours wants allait, not est allé.

sentences.display: Je ne fume plus depuis deux ans
sentences.cue: I stopped smoking two years ago
sentences.literal: I not smoke more since two years

words.note: Written whole because L2-M9 owns bare plus as the comparative. Here plus is the negator and only the ne in front of the verb tells the two apart.

sentences.trap: The same four letters mean more and no more. plus facile is more easy; ne … plus is not any more. The ne is not decoration here — it is the entire difference.
sentences.sound: zhuh nuh fewm PLEW duh-ZAHN. As a negator the s of plus is silent; as the comparative it is often heard. That one consonant is the spoken signal.

variations.display: Aujourd'hui, je ne fume plus
variations.cue: These days I don't smoke any more
variations.changed: the now word moves to the front

variations.display: Je ne fume plus depuis trois ans
variations.cue: I stopped smoking three years ago

mistake.display: Je fume plus depuis deux ans
mistake.why: without the ne this reads as I smoke more — the comparative. Dropping it does not soften the sentence, it reverses it.

sentences.usage: Saying a habit is behind you, which in French is a present-tense sentence, not a past one.

sentences.display: Aujourd'hui, on ne se voit plus
sentences.cue: These days we don't see each other any more
sentences.literal: Today, one not oneself sees more

words.note: The now word for a period rather than a date. Beside an imparfait clause it is what makes the contrast readable.

words.cue: we don't see each other any more
words.note: Whole, for the same reason as je ne fume plus: bare plus is L2-M9's. The se here is each other, not oneself.

sentences.trap: English needs each other and French does not — the se carries it. A learner adding a translation for it produces a pronoun French has nowhere to put.
sentences.sound: oh-zhoor-DWEE, ohn nuh suh vwah PLEW. aujourd'hui is three syllables ending on a long wee; the s of plus stays silent.

variations.display: Maintenant, on ne se voit plus
variations.cue: Now we don't see each other any more

variations.display: On ne se voit plus depuis deux ans
variations.cue: We haven't seen each other for two years

mistake.why: with no ne this says we see each other more, which is the opposite news. ne … plus is one negator in two pieces and both are written.

sentences.usage: Saying a friendship has faded, without saying anything unkind about why.
sentences.mnemonic: se is each other; plus needs its ne.

sentences.display: J'irais bien au cinéma, mais je dois travailler
sentences.cue: I'd quite like to go to the cinema, but I have to work
sentences.literal: I-would-go well to-the cinema, but I must work

words.note: L3-M4's conditional, not an imparfait. English says would for both; this one is a hypothesis, and on allait is the habit.

sentences.trap: This is the module's whole hinge. We would go every summer and I would go if I could share one English word and take two different French tenses. Ask which one the sentence means before you pick.
sentences.sound: zhee-REH byan oh see-nay-MAH, meh zhuh dwah tra-vah-YAY. j'irais is two syllables, zhee-reh, and the bien after it is unstressed.

variations.display: J'irais bien à la mer, mais je dois travailler
variations.cue: I'd quite like to go to the sea, but I have to work

variations.display: J'irais bien au marché, mais je n'ai pas le temps
variations.cue: I'd quite like to go to the market, but I don't have time

mistake.display: J'allais bien au cinéma, mais je dois travailler
mistake.why: j'allais is the habit — I used to go — which cannot sit in front of but I have to work today. A wish that has not happened takes j'irais.

sentences.usage: Turning something down while making it clear you would rather not be turning it down.

sentences.display: Avant, la vie était plus facile
sentences.literal: Before, the life was more easy

words.note: Life as a whole, the way a period is lived. It is the noun this module's contrast is usually about.
The same form for a masculine or a feminine noun, so nothing agrees. Its comparative is L2-M9's plus facile.

sentences.trap: plus facile is more easy, with no ne anywhere. Set beside S05's je ne fume plus it is the clean demonstration that the word itself decides nothing: the ne does.
sentences.sound: ah-VAHN, lah vee ay-TEH plew fah-SEEL. Here the s of plus is often heard, because it is the comparative and not the negator.

variations.display: Aujourd'hui, la vie est plus facile
variations.cue: Life is easier these days
variations.changed: the now half of the same claim

variations.display: Avant, la vie était moins facile
variations.cue: Life used to be harder

mistake.display: Avant, la vie ne était plus facile
mistake.why: adding a ne turns more easy into not easy any more, which is a different sentence — and the ne would elide to n' in any case.

sentences.usage: The line every generation says about the one before it.
sentences.mnemonic: plus with ne negates; plus alone compares.

sentences.display: Tout a changé depuis dix ans
sentences.cue: Everything has changed in the last ten years
sentences.literal: All has changed since ten years

words.note: Everything, standing alone as a subject. The final t is silent, and it is the same tout that opens L4-M10's tout à coup.
The participle of changer, on avoir. This is the one sentence in the module that names a completed change rather than a standing state.

sentences.trap: English reaches for a perfect and a for — everything has changed for ten years — and gets the preposition wrong. French keeps depuis, which is L3-M7's, and it means over the last ten years.
sentences.sound: too tah shahn-ZHAY duh-pwee dee-ZAHN. tout a links across the t; dix ans links across the x, heard as a z.

variations.display: Tout a changé depuis deux ans
variations.cue: Everything has changed in the last two years

variations.display: Ici, tout a changé depuis dix ans
variations.cue: Here, everything has changed in the last ten years

mistake.why: the imparfait would make the changing itself the standing state. What is meant is the finished result you can see now, which takes a changé.

sentences.usage: Summing up a decade in five words, usually before the details.
sentences.mnemonic: A state stands; a change lands.

sentences.display: À l'époque, je ne pouvais pas travailler ici
sentences.cue: Back then, I couldn't work here
sentences.literal: At the-time, I not could not to-work here

words.note: The imparfait of pouvoir, for an ability you had or lacked over a period. Not a single failed attempt — that would be the passé composé.

sentences.trap: English could is a past and a conditional at once — I couldn't then, I couldn't possibly now. je ne pouvais pas is only the first. The second is L3-M4's conditional and belongs to another sentence.
sentences.sound: ah lay-POK, zhuh nuh poo-VEH pah tra-vah-YAY ee-SEE. pouvais rhymes with j'étais and takes the same open eh.

variations.display: Autrefois, je ne pouvais pas travailler ici
variations.cue: In the old days, I couldn't work here

variations.display: À l'époque, je ne pouvais pas travailler à Paris
variations.cue: Back then, I couldn't work in Paris

mistake.display: À l'époque, je n'ai pas pu travailler ici
mistake.why: je n'ai pas pu is one occasion on which it did not come off. A standing impossibility across a period is je ne pouvais pas.

sentences.usage: Explaining a rule, a permit or a circumstance that used to stand in your way and no longer does.
